result.title: LINK: Lightweight and Inductive Node-to-Node Propagation Rule Learning for Traffic Kriging
result.summary: Spatio-temporal traffic kriging aims to reconstruct traffic time series at unobserved locations with no historical traffic observations by leveraging spatial and temporal dependencies across the road network. Existing Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based approaches primarily rely on neighborhood aggregation to capture spatial dependencies, thereby modeling traffic interactions implicitly and making it difficult to accurately recover traffic magnitudes at locations without historical observations. To address this limitation, we propose LINK, a Lightweight and Inductive Node-to-node propagation rule learning paradigm for traffic Kriging. LINK introduces three key designs: 1) a propagation-centric traffic kriging paradigm that explicitly learns a shared node-to-node transition rule; 2) a context-aware Spectral Propagation Network that performs traffic-state propagation in both the spectral and time domains; and 3) TraffiKrig, a realistic traffic kriging benchmark that preserves heterogeneous road-segment characteristics and road-specific metadata while enabling systematic comparison of representative kriging methods under a unified metadata-enhanced setting. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LINK achieves strong reconstruction accuracy and computational efficiency. Compared with the strongest baseline on each subset, LINK achieves an average MAE reduction of 54.7% over original baselines. LINK also achieves substantial efficiency improvements, reducing training time by 66.5% and inference time by 86.6% compared with the fastest competing methods. Zero-shot experiments further demonstrate the transferability of the learned propagation rule across regions.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 LINK，用显式学习的共享节点间传播规则替代 GNN 邻域聚合来重建未观测路段的交通时序，包含谱域与时域上的上下文感知传播网络，并构建配套基准 TraffiKrig。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「共享转移规则 + 显式状态传播」的轻量设计可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态的迭代更新与计算成本权衡提供线索，但任务域与多模态推理相距较远，迁移价值需核查。
